B1: capability row for the llm-session-wrapper deep-tier model id

Route TradingAgents' deep reasoning nodes (research manager, portfolio manager)
through the subscription-backed llm-session-wrapper instead of a metered API.

The wrapper is an OpenAI-compatible shim over text-only coding CLIs (agy/claude):
it cannot perform tool calls or response_format structured output. Add one additive
capability row keying the wrapper model id `gemini-3.1-pro-high` to
preferred_structured_method="none" (a new _WRAPPER_TEXT_ONLY constant). Without it,
the unknown id falls through to _DEFAULT (function_calling), so each deep node makes
a wasted structured attempt plus a free-text fallback — two slow CLI calls per node.
With it, bind_structured() returns None at agent creation and the node makes a single
free-text call.

Repoint itself is config-only (deep_llm_provider=openai_compatible,
deep_backend_url=http://localhost:11500/v1, deep_think_llm=gemini-3.1-pro-high) and is
documented in .env.example for standalone use; this project drives it from the
orchestrator's deep-tier config.

Additive only — no edits to existing capability rows; existing tests pass unchanged
(24 capabilities tests green, incl. 3 new ones for the wrapper row).

feat(backtest): momentum_v1 native strategy (SDK strategy library)

Third native strategy, a third distinct archetype: rate-of-change
momentum. Enter in the direction of a strong recent move (|ROC| over
roc_period beyond roc_threshold %) for a FIXED-R outcome (ATR stop + ATR
target, no trailing) — mechanically distinct from the breakout (channel +
trailing) and mean-reversion (fade the mean) packages. Long & short.

Registry-driven, so it joins the run picker + optimizer + portfolio with no
plumbing. MOMENTUM_V1_PARAMS: roc_period, roc_threshold, stop_atr_mult,
target_atr_mult, risk_pct, allow_short. 6 tests (registered, defaults,
enters long on up-momentum, high threshold suppresses weak momentum,
deterministic). momentum + mean-reversion + trend + equivalence suites 22
passed; ruff clean.

Native strategy library now: trend_following_v1 (breakout), mean_reversion_v1
(fade), momentum_v1 (ROC).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(backtest): htf_momentum_v1 — multi-TF-confirmed strategy + job wiring

The first real consumer of the multi-timeframe context (ctx.htf, built in
P3.7 but until now only unit-tested). ROC momentum entries taken only in
the direction of the HIGHER timeframe's trend — longs blocked when the HTF
is below its mean, shorts when above ("trade with the bigger tide"). Trades
unconfirmed when no HTF is available (warm-up / not configured), so it runs
anywhere.

- strategies.HtfMomentumV1 declares htf_timeframes = (D1, W1) and reads the
  coarsest available ctx.htf snapshot for its bias. Registered as
  htf_momentum_v1 → auto in picker/optimizer/portfolio.
- run_job now activates multi-TF in PROD: it reads a strategy's declared
  htf_timeframes, keeps those strictly coarser than the run timeframe, and
  passes them to the engine (populates ctx.htf). Strategies without the
  attribute are unaffected (htf=None). _StreamingEngine already forwards
  **kwargs, so no wrapper change needed.

3 tests incl. the key one: on a daily-downtrend / hourly-bounce series the
HTF filter strictly cuts counter-trend longs vs the unconfirmed run while
still taking with-trend shorts. HTF + job + momentum + equivalence suites
52 passed; ruff clean.

Native library now: trend_following_v1, mean_reversion_v1, momentum_v1,
ma_crossover_v1, htf_momentum_v1.

feat(app): /analyze + /stream — wrap TradingAgents with HTTP + SSE

Implements the user-facing endpoints for the Lyceum Fund Python service.
After this lands, the Node-side worker can POST /analyze to kick off a
TradingAgents run, and the dashboard can subscribe to /stream/{runId}
for live per-agent progress.

Architecture:
- app/services/trading_agents_runner.py orchestrates a run end-to-end —
  constructs TradingAgentsGraph (with memory_log_path=None to disable
  upstream file persistence), bypasses propagate() to control the
  astream() loop, injects a LangChain callback that writes agent_reports
  rows + publishes events to Redis pub-sub.
- app/services/callbacks.py — AsyncCallbackHandler. on_chain_start fires
  agent_started event, on_chain_end persists the chains output to
  agent_reports + fires agent_finished. Heuristic name normalizer drops
  Chain/Agent suffixes from serialized chain names.
- app/services/pubsub.py — generic Redis pub-sub helpers. Channel
  convention run:<runId>. DONE_SENTINEL marks stream end.
- app/services/stream_token.py — HMAC-signed compact tokens for SSE auth.
  Format: base64url(payload).hex(hmac_sha256(payload, HMAC_SHARED_SECRET))
  with payload {runId, exp}. Browser EventSource cant send headers so
  the query-param token replaces HMAC headers for browser streams.
- app/routes/analyze.py — POST /analyze. HMAC-auth via existing
  middleware. Idempotent on runId so Node-side retries dont duplicate.
  Schedules a FastAPI BackgroundTask; returns 202 immediately.
- app/routes/stream.py — GET /stream/{run_id}?token=... SSE feed. Token
  verified server-side. Subscribes to Redis pub-sub, forwards each
  event as data: <json> records. Closes on DONE_SENTINEL with an
  event: close record.

v1 uses FastAPI BackgroundTasks for the analyze pipeline — see TT-286
for the planned migration to a dedicated Arq worker service when

fix: stop leaking OpenAI base_url into non-OpenAI provider clients

Default config had backend_url='https://api.openai.com/v1' which was
forwarded to every provider client, including Google. ChatGoogleGenerativeAI
constructed requests against that base, producing malformed URLs like
https://api.openai.com/v1/v1beta/models/gemini-2.5-flash:generateContent
that 404 with empty body.

Discovered while running propagate() against Gemini end-to-end. The
structured-output smoke worked because that path constructed the LLM
without going through the factory and without forwarding backend_url;
propagate() goes through TradingAgentsGraph.__init__ which forwards
config['backend_url'] to every provider.

Fix: default to None. Each provider client falls back to its own
endpoint (api.openai.com for OpenAI via _PROVIDER_CONFIG, Gemini's
default for Google, and so on). The CLI flow already sets backend_url
explicitly per provider when the user picks one, so that path is
unchanged.

fix(security): validate ticker symbols before using them as path components

Three call sites interpolate the ticker directly into a filesystem path:

- tradingagents/dataflows/stockstats_utils.py::load_ohlcv builds
  os.path.join(cache_dir, f"{symbol}-YFin-data-{start}-{end}.csv")
- tradingagents/graph/checkpointer.py::_db_path builds
  Path(data_dir) / "checkpoints" / f"{ticker.upper()}.db"
- tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py::_log_state builds
  Path(results_dir) / self.ticker / "TradingAgentsStrategy_logs"

A ticker containing path separators or "..", e.g. "../../../tmp/x",
escapes the configured cache, checkpoint, or results directory. The
ticker reaches these sites from user CLI input and from LLM tool
calls — the latter is reachable when fetched news content (yfinance,
alpha_vantage) carries prompt-injection text that steers the agent into
calling get_indicators / get_stock_data with a malicious symbol.

Add a single safe_ticker_component() helper in dataflows/utils.py that
allows only [A-Za-z0-9._^-] (covers AAPL, BRK.A, BRK-B, 0700.HK,
7203.T, ^GSPC) and rejects anything else. Apply it at each path-build
site. Existing tests use ticker="TEST" / "AAPL" / "7203.T" — all pass
the validator unchanged. Added tests/test_safe_ticker_component.py.

feat(backtest): P3.1 — PortfolioReplay k-way timestamp merge (track T4)

The foundation for multi-symbol / multi-timeframe backtests: merge N
per-symbol BarReplays onto one master clock (the sorted union of every

fix: cash_sweep target_cash_pct from config, defaults to min_cash_pct

Audit finding (Important): cash_sweep hardcoded target_cash_pct=0.05 while
min_cash_pct is config-driven. A deployment that raised min_cash_pct (e.g.

Defaulting to min_cash_pct keeps the soft target tied to the hard floor;
operators may still set target_cash_pct > min_cash_pct for a buffer.

fix(yfinance): reconstruct fundamentals point-in-time to fix look-ahead bias

yfinance's Ticker.info ignores the curr_date a backtest passes — it always
returns *live* values (current market cap, TTM ratios, 52-week ranges,
moving averages, dividend yield). On a 2024-05-10 NVDA backtest the
fundamentals analyst was therefore being shown the April 2026 snapshot:
Market Cap $5.09T (actual May 2024: ~$2.3T), Revenue TTM $215.94B (actual:
~$80B). Bull/Bear debate downstream cited the poisoned figures.

Fix:

* Split the report into stable structural fields (name, sector, industry,
  beta) which are date-insensitive, and live-snapshot fields which are
  not. _is_historical_curr_date decides which mode applies.

* For historical curr_dates, reconstruct the snapshot fields PIT-correctly
  in a new yf_pit_derivations module from data yfinance does expose with
  proper time indexing:
    - Ticker.history(start, end) -> 52-wk H/L, 50/200-day MAs, close at
      curr_date
    - quarterly_income_stmt / quarterly_balance_sheet / quarterly_cashflow
      filtered to fiscal periods <= curr_date -> TTM revenue/gross
      profit/EBITDA/net income/FCF, margins, ROE/ROA, debt/equity,
      current ratio, book value
    - get_shares_full -> market cap = close x shares-outstanding
    - dividends -> trailing-365d yield

* Forward-looking fields (Forward EPS, Forward P/E, PEG Ratio) are
  intentionally not reconstructed — they are analyst projections, not
  historical fact, and have no PIT-correct yfinance source. Beta is
  preserved from info as a (stable) structural field.

* Robust to sparse data: TTM requires 4 non-NaN quarters <= curr_date,
  otherwise the field is omitted rather than published as a partial sum.
  Line-item lookup uses synonym lists (Total Revenue / TotalRevenue, Net
  Income / Net Income Common Stockholders / etc.) so reports with
  different label conventions still derive correctly. Derivation failures
  degrade gracefully — the structural fields still publish.

* Header note explicitly flags PIT mode and lists how many of the
  reconstructable fields were derived, so the LLM agent reasons about a
  known reconstruction instead of either trusting poisoned numbers or
  hallucinating around a silent gap.

import the next time anyone touches an analyst or the data-vendor
interface. Declaring `__all__` is a zero-runtime-cost annotation that
makes the public surface explicit and tells lint/type tools to leave
these imports alone.

fix(reddit): go RSS-first with 429 backoff and robust transport errors

The JSON search endpoint is reliably WAF-blocked (403) for public clients, so
probing it on every call doubled request volume against Reddit's per-IP rate
limit and tripped 429 on the RSS fallback, blanking the sentiment feed. Fetch
the Atom/RSS feed directly (JSON kept as an opt-in path that still degrades to
RSS on 403), back off once on a 429 honouring Retry-After, and pace requests a
little wider. Also broaden the error handling to catch http.client chunked
transfer errors (IncompleteRead/BadStatusLine) alongside OSError, which on their
own slipped through and crashed the pipeline.

fix(reddit): pace requests with adaptive rate limiter to prevent 429 cascading

Adds a module-level rate limiter (_pace_request / _on_rate_limited) that enforces a minimum gap between Reddit requests across all subreddits. On a 429 the gap doubles (capped at 30s) and decays back to baseline after 30s of quiet. Previously, fetching 3 subreddits for the same ticker hit Reddit's per-IP rate limit on every subreddit because each had its own separate backoff.

Add async DB log handler — Python logs → system_logs table

The system_logs table existed but was always empty because log_service.py
was never called anywhere. The Logs page in the frontend showed nothing.

into system_logs automatically:

    error call in backend.services.*, backend.api.*, etc. is captured

  - Graceful drain: db_log_handler.stop() flushes remaining entries on
    shutdown

created), db_log_handler.stop() on shutdown.

feat: structured-output Portfolio Manager + 5-tier rating consistency (#434)

Three related changes that take the rating pipeline from heuristic-only
to type-safe at the source.

1) Research Manager prompt now uses the same 5-tier scale (Buy /
   Overweight / Hold / Underweight / Sell) as the Portfolio Manager,
   signal_processing, and the memory log.  The prior 3-tier wording
   (Buy / Sell / Hold) was the only remaining inconsistency in the
   pipeline.

2) Centralise the 5-tier vocabulary and the heuristic prose-rating
   parser into tradingagents/agents/utils/rating.py.  Both the memory
   log and the signal processor now share the same parser instead of
   duplicating regex and word-walker logic.

3) Make structured output a first-class part of the Portfolio Manager's
   primary call.  The PM uses llm.with_structured_output(PortfolioDecision)
   so each provider's native structured-output mode (json_schema for
   OpenAI/xAI, response_schema for Gemini, tool-use for Anthropic,
   function_calling for OpenAI-compatible providers) yields a typed
   Pydantic instance directly.  A render helper turns that instance back
   into the same markdown shape downstream consumers (memory log, CLI
   display, saved reports) already expect, so no other code has to know
   the PM now produces structured output.  Providers without structured
   support fall back gracefully to free-text + the deterministic
   heuristic.

   The previous SignalProcessor had been making a second LLM call to
   re-extract the rating from the PM's prose; that round-trip is now
   eliminated.  SignalProcessor is a thin adapter over parse_rating(),
   makes zero LLM calls, and stays for backwards compatibility with
   process_signal() callers.

Schema (PortfolioDecision) captures rating + executive_summary +
investment_thesis + optional price_target + time_horizon, with field
descriptions doubling as output instructions.  Agent prose remains the
primary artifact; structured output is layered onto the PM only because
it is the one agent whose output has machine-readable downstream
consumers.

15 new tests cover the heuristic parser (markdown-bold edge cases that

fallback path, and that SignalProcessor never invokes the LLM.  Full

feat(ops): NAS deploy + maintenance scripts with credential isolation

Adds a credential pattern that lets Claude operate the NAS deployment
without ever seeing the user's SSH credentials. Pattern:

- ``scripts/nas/credentials.local.example`` is a committed template.
- ``scripts/nas/credentials.local`` is the user's filled-in copy. It's
  in .gitignore and Claude is instructed never to read it.
- The scripts in this directory ``source`` it to get connection info,
  so creds become env vars in the script's process — never on stdout,
  never visible to Claude's tools (which see only the script's output).

Scripts:

- ``nas-cmd.sh "<cmd>"`` — run any command on the NAS (used by the others)
- ``deploy.sh`` — first-time clone + build + start, idempotent
- ``upgrade.sh`` — pull + rebuild + restart (the routine update path)
- ``restart.sh`` — kick the container without rebuilding (e.g. after .env edits)
- ``status.sh`` — compose ps, container health, image, git SHA, data dir size
- ``logs.sh`` — tail the gui service logs
- ``rollback.sh <sha|previous>`` — roll back to a prior commit and rebuild

All support either SSH-key auth (recommended) or password auth via
sshpass. Path-expansion handles ``~`` in NAS_SSH_KEY.

``OPERATIONS.md`` at the repo root is the master reference. It documents
the credential pattern, the NAS layout, the script index, common Claude
prompts that map to scripts, and troubleshooting recipes. The user can
paste sections of OPERATIONS.md back to Claude when asking for changes.

fix: cash_sweep target_cash_pct from config, defaults to min_cash_pct

Audit finding (Important): cash_sweep hardcoded target_cash_pct=0.05 while
min_cash_pct is config-driven. A deployment that raised min_cash_pct (e.g.
to 0.10) would have its operator-intent silently violated — sweep would
keep pushing cash toward the 5% target, leaving the reserve below intent.
The hard floor was never breached, but the soft target no longer matched
the deployed policy.

Fix: target_cash_pct = float(config.get("target_cash_pct", min_cash_pct)).
Defaulting to min_cash_pct keeps the soft target tied to the hard floor;
operators may still set target_cash_pct > min_cash_pct for a buffer.

  min_cash_pct=0.10 leaves a 10% reserve, not 5%.

fix(server): use regularMarketPreviousClose for change_pct

yfinance fast_info exposes two previous-close values:
  - previousClose: an intraday/adjusted value
  - regularMarketPreviousClose: the prior REGULAR session's close, the
    standard reference used by every financial site ("today's change"
    vs yesterday's close)

The previous code keyed on previousClose, which can differ by 0.5-1%
on real tickers (NVDA, TSLA, MSFT) and yields a visibly wrong
change_pct. Example: TSLA lastPrice=424.04 with the old code showed
+0.53% (vs previousClose 421.78) when the correct value is +0.08%
(vs regularMarketPreviousClose 423.74).

Now prefers regularMarketPreviousClose, falls back to previousClose
for tickers/sessions that don't populate it.

feat(llm): generic agentic-CLI provider base + Gemini CLI

Generalizes the recently-added claude_code provider into a shared
SubprocessChatModel abstract base that any headless agentic CLI can plug
into, then adds a working second concrete provider (Google Gemini CLI).

Why: many agent CLIs (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, future ones) follow the
same pattern — spawn the binary in headless mode, send a prompt, parse
JSON output — and the user's local OAuth login provides auth without an
API key. Sharing the machinery makes it cheap to add new ones.

What's shared in tradingagents/llm_clients/subprocess_chat_base.py:
- per-call subprocess spawning with isolation (run from temp cwd, env
  sanitization hook, custom timeout)
- chat-history rendering: SystemMessages collapsed into the system
  prompt, everything else role-tagged in the user prompt with
  ### user / ### assistant / ### tool[name] markers
- JSON-envelope tool-calling protocol — assistant emits
  {"tool_calls": [...]} which we parse out (with tolerant brace-matching
  for prose-wrapped responses) so langgraph's ToolNode runs project tools
- structured output via Pydantic schemas (subclass exposes its own
  --json-schema-style flag, base normalizes the result)

Subclass-specific bits each provider implements:
- _binary_name / _binary_env_var — how to find the CLI
- _build_command — argv + flags
- _parse_response — pull (text, structured) out of stdout
- _subprocess_input / _subprocess_env (optional) — stdin shaping and
  env var sanitization (e.g. strip ANTHROPIC_API_KEY when forcing
  subscription routing)

Concrete providers:
- ChatClaudeCode — refactored to inherit from base; behavior unchanged.
  Still uses --setting-sources "" / --strict-mcp-config /
  --disable-slash-commands / --tools "" / --system-prompt for clean
  per-agent isolation from the user's CLAUDE.md, MCP servers, etc.
- ChatGeminiCli (new) — `gemini -p` with --approval-mode plan +
  --allowed-mcp-server-names "" for read-only, MCP-isolated execution.
  Inlines system prompt into the prompt argument since Gemini has no
  --system-prompt flag.

feat(dataflows): CLS, Cninfo, Eastmoney news vendors + auto-router

Adds three news vendors covering HK and CN A-share (SH / SZ) tickers:

  * Eastmoney  — editorial Chinese-language news (HK / SH / SZ)
  * CLS        — Cailianshe flash-news stream (HK / SH / SZ)
  * Cninfo     — official CSRC corporate disclosures (SH / SZ only)

The vendors are wired into route_to_vendor via a ticker-suffix
auto-router. When data_vendors.news_data = "auto" (now the default),
the router dispatches:

  * .HK            -> eastmoney + cls
  * .SS / .SH / .SZ -> eastmoney + cls + cninfo
  * everything else -> yfinance (existing behaviour)

Multi-vendor calls run sequentially and concatenate non-empty results
as Markdown blocks separated by horizontal rules. Per-vendor failures
and "[Vendor skip — ...]" markers are dropped from the merge so the
analyst sees whichever sources succeeded; if all sources fail or skip,
we fall through to yfinance as a final safety net.

Each vendor call goes through the per-vendor cache added in the
preceding commit — daily buckets for editorial / flash news, weekly
buckets (ISO-week-Monday-keyed) for Cninfo since disclosures spike at
quarter-end.

Adds akshare>=1.18 as a runtime dep (Eastmoney / Cninfo backends).
Imported lazily inside the vendors so users analysing only US tickers
pay no import cost.

Tests cover routing, the multi-vendor merge, skip-marker filtering,
cache hit/miss, and Cninfo's two known schema shapes (公告链接 vs
announcementId+orgId). All vendor calls are mocked at the akshare
import boundary — no live network.

fix(y_finance): make suppress_yfinance_warnings thread-safe

The previous implementation redirected sys.stderr to /dev/null using a
context manager. This is not thread-safe: 8 concurrent scanner threads each
mutate sys.stderr, and when one thread's context manager closes the devnull
file, another thread that captured devnull as its saved stderr attempts to
write to the closed fd and raises "I/O operation on closed file".

This corrupted sys.stderr state caused _fetch_batch_prices to fail and
all per-ticker get_stock_price fallback calls to return None, resulting in
every candidate being dropped with "no data available".

Fix by suppressing at the Python logging level instead of redirecting
sys.stderr. Logger.setLevel() is protected by internal locks and is safe
to call from concurrent threads.

* ci: add test/lint/smoke workflow, declare python-dotenv, recommend Python 3.12

GitHub Actions: pytest across Python 3.10-3.13, a clean-install import smoke
that catches undeclared runtime deps, and a strict Ruff gate (standard rule set)
scoped to the files each PR changes. Declares python-dotenv (imported by the CLI
but previously undeclared) and adds a [dev] extra. Recommends Python 3.12 for
setup, verified from a clean isolated install.

* fix(data): normalize symbols on the identity and reflection paths

resolve_instrument_identity and the reflection return lookup queried Yahoo with
the raw ticker, so broker/forex/commodity symbols (XAUUSD, BTCUSD, EURUSD)
failed identity or could mismatch the priced instrument even though the price
path already normalized them. Route both through normalize_symbol (#983, #984).

* fix(cli): unify ticker handling with the data-path symbol normalizer

The CLI validated, normalized, and classified tickers with its own logic that
diverged from the data layer: it rejected '=' symbols like GC=F (#980),
classified BTCUSD as a stock (#981), and accepted unpriceable BTC-USDT (#982).
Route the CLI through normalize_symbol (now mapping USDT/USDC crypto quotes to
Yahoo's -USD pair), so validation, classification, and pricing agree.

* fix(data): respect the configured vendor chain and log vendor failures

The router silently extended every request to all available vendors regardless
of config, so an explicit single-vendor choice still fell back to others and
returned data from an unexpected source (#988, #289), and serious primary-vendor
errors were swallowed without a trace (#989). The configured vendor list is now
the exact chain (list several for ordered fallback; "default" uses all), unknown
vendors raise, and swallowed vendor errors are logged. Adds an autouse config
isolation fixture so vendor config can't leak between tests.

* fix(data): include the requested end date in yfinance fetches

yfinance treats end as exclusive, so get_YFin_data_online dropped the requested
end_date row and load_ohlcv dropped the current day. Request one day past the
end so the range is inclusive (look-ahead is still prevented by the curr_date
filter; the header still shows the requested range). Also correct the load_ohlcv
docstring to the 5-year window it actually downloads.

* fix(cli): correct invalid escape sequence in confirm_ollama_endpoint docstring

The docstring used \` (an invalid escape that raises SyntaxWarning and will
become a SyntaxError); use plain backticks.

* fix(data): add Alpha Vantage request timeout and stop mislabeling bad keys

Alpha Vantage requests had no timeout (a stall could hang the run) and any
notice mentioning "API key" was raised as a rate limit — so an invalid/missing
key was mislabeled and silently treated as transient. Add a 30s request timeout
and classify rate-limit phrasing before key errors (rate-limit notices also
mention "API key"), surfacing a bad key as a real configuration error.

* fix(data): keep future/undated news out of historical windows

The yfinance news date filter only ran when an article had a parsed date, so
flat-format and undated articles bypassed it and leaked future news into
historical/backtest runs. Parse the flat providerPublishTime, apply one
look-ahead-safe window rule across ticker and global news (undated kept only
when the window reaches the present), and return an informative message when
everything is filtered out.

* fix(graph): register get_verified_market_snapshot in the market ToolNode

The market analyst is bound to call get_verified_market_snapshot and its prompt
requires it as the source of truth, but the tool was missing from the market
ToolNode executor — so the call failed and the model reported it "unavailable"
and skipped verification. Register it (with a regression guard) so the snapshot
actually runs and grounds the report.

* feat(llm): unify OpenAI-compatible providers behind a registry + generic endpoint

The OpenAI-compatible family (openai, xAI, DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM, MiniMax,
OpenRouter, Ollama) all speak the same Chat Completions API and differ only by
base_url, key, and two narrow wire-format quirks already isolated in subclasses.
Replace the scattered base-URL dict, key handling, and client-class branches with
one ProviderSpec registry that get_llm and the factory drive off; provider quirks
stay in their subclasses. Add a generic "openai_compatible" provider for any
OpenAI-compatible server (vLLM, LM Studio, llama.cpp, relays) via backend_url +
optional key — adding a provider is now one registry row. Native Anthropic/Google
keep their own clients (genuinely different APIs). Also fixes the env backend URL
being ignored when the provider was chosen interactively (#978).

* feat(llm): add NVIDIA NIM, Kimi, Groq, and Mistral providers

Each is a one-row entry in the OpenAI-compatible provider registry (base_url,
key env, CLI option); the model is user-specified since they serve many models.

* feat(llm): add Amazon Bedrock as a first-class provider

Bedrock uses the Converse API (langchain-aws) and the AWS credential chain, so

* feat(data): add FRED macro indicators as an optional vendor

Surface Federal Reserve Economic Data (rates, inflation, labor, growth) to the
news analyst via a new get_macro_indicators tool and a macro_data vendor
category. Friendly aliases (cpi, unemployment, fed_funds_rate, 10y_treasury,
yield_curve, ...) map to FRED series IDs; raw series IDs are accepted too. The
report gives the latest value, change over the window, and a recent observation
table. Windowing is lookahead-safe (observation_end = curr_date), missing values
are skipped, and a missing FRED_API_KEY surfaces as a clear not-configured
condition through the vendor router rather than a crash.

* feat(data): add Polymarket prediction markets as a keyless vendor

Surface live, market-implied probabilities for forward-looking events (Fed
decisions, recession, elections, geopolitics, crypto) to the news analyst via a
new get_prediction_markets tool and a prediction_markets vendor category. Backed
by Polymarket's public Gamma API (no key). Results are filtered to open,
forward-looking markets (closed and past-dated events excluded), ranked by
traded volume, and rendered with implied probability, volume, resolution date,
and the recent move. External errors degrade to a clear unavailable message
rather than interrupting the analyst.

* refactor(data): unify vendor errors under a VendorError hierarchy

Every condition where a vendor cannot return usable data now derives from a
single VendorError base (errors.py): NoMarketDataError, VendorRateLimitError,
and VendorNotConfiguredError (still a ValueError for back-compat). Vendor-named
errors subclass the generic bases, and the router catches the base types, so a
new vendor needs no new except clause. Not-configured now has explicit
try-next-vendor handling instead of falling through the generic catch-all. The
number of error types tracks the number of distinct router reactions, not the
number of causes.

* fix(data): reject stale yfinance OHLCV instead of reporting wrong prices

yfinance intermittently returns a year-old partial frame (e.g. June 2025 rows
for a June 2026 request) that still has rows and a Close, so it passed the
empty-check and silently fed a wrong close price and indicators into the report
(#1021). Add a freshness guard that rejects a frame whose latest row is far
older than the requested date, on both the raw OHLCV path and the indicator
path. It raises the existing NoMarketDataError with a stale-specific detail, so
the vendor router's try-next-vendor and single unavailable-signal handling apply
unchanged; the sentinel now surfaces that detail so the agent reports the
specific reason rather than fabricating a value.

* fix(reddit): go RSS-first with 429 backoff and robust transport errors

The JSON search endpoint is reliably WAF-blocked (403) for public clients, so
probing it on every call doubled request volume against Reddit's per-IP rate
limit and tripped 429 on the RSS fallback, blanking the sentiment feed. Fetch
the Atom/RSS feed directly (JSON kept as an opt-in path that still degrades to
RSS on 403), back off once on a 429 honouring Retry-After, and pace requests a
little wider. Also broaden the error handling to catch http.client chunked
transfer errors (IncompleteRead/BadStatusLine) alongside OSError, which on their
own slipped through and crashed the pipeline.

* fix(data): catch http.client transport errors in StockTwits

A truncated/incomplete chunked response raises http.client exceptions
(IncompleteRead/BadStatusLine) that are not OSErrors, so they bypassed the
existing handler and crashed the analysis. Broaden the catch so the fetch
degrades to its placeholder string like every other transport failure.

fix(llm): retry once when claude-code returns error-only partial text

The full-graph smoke run surfaced a silent failure: when the CLI's
upstream socket dropped mid-stream, the SDK delivered an "API Error:
The socket connection was closed unexpectedly..." string as the last
AssistantMessage TextBlock before tearing down. Our partial-text
recovery dutifully collected those 134 chars and returned them as the
"reply", so the news_analyst and fundamentals_analyst silently wrote
nonsense reports into ``news_report`` / ``fundamentals_report`` and
the downstream pipeline ran on corrupted state.

The streaming loop is now extracted into a ``_run_query`` helper and
``_aquery`` invokes it twice when the returned text matches the
documented soft-failure shape — short, opens with a known CLI/API
error marker, and was not flagged ``api_error_status=429``. Hard rate
limits skip the retry because the rate-limit window is measured in
minutes (immediate retry is wasted quota). On a double failure we
raise ``RuntimeError`` so a corrupted analyst surface fails loudly
instead of pretending it succeeded.

12 new tests cover the heuristic (empty / short-with-prefix /
short-without-prefix / long-with-prefix / 429-skip / 500-still-retries)
and the retry flow (retry-then-succeed / double-failure-raises /
429-no-retry / clean-first-attempt-no-retry). 277 tests pass total
(was 265).

fix(y_finance): make suppress_yfinance_warnings thread-safe

The previous implementation redirected sys.stderr to /dev/null using a
context manager. This is not thread-safe: 8 concurrent scanner threads each
mutate sys.stderr, and when one thread's context manager closes the devnull
file, another thread that captured devnull as its saved stderr attempts to
write to the closed fd and raises "I/O operation on closed file".

This corrupted sys.stderr state caused _fetch_batch_prices to fail and
all per-ticker get_stock_price fallback calls to return None, resulting in
every candidate being dropped with "no data available".

Fix by suppressing at the Python logging level instead of redirecting
sys.stderr. Logger.setLevel() is protected by internal locks and is safe
to call from concurrent threads.

The autouse _dummy_api_keys fixture used os.environ.get(var, "placeholder"),

for public clients -- the module docstring already documents this (#862). Yet
it was still attempted for every subreddit before falling back to RSS, so each
fetch made ~2x the requests against Reddit's per-IP rate limit and routinely
tripped HTTP 429 on the RSS fallback, blanking the sentiment data entirely.

Reproduced from a single egress IP: `/search.json` -> 403, `/search.rss` ->
200; a normal 3-subreddit run fires 6 requests in ~1.6s (the 403s return
instantly, defeating the inter-request delay) and 429s on the 2nd/3rd RSS call.

- Default per-subreddit fetch now goes straight to RSS, halving request volume.
  The JSON path is preserved as `_fetch_subreddit_json` for the day the WAF
  relaxes or an OAuth token is wired in.
- The RSS path backs off once on 429 (honouring `Retry-After`, capped at 30s)
  before giving up, so a transient burst no longer blanks the feed.
- Pace per-subreddit requests 0.4s -> 1.0s.

Tests: retarget the JSON-fallback test at `_fetch_subreddit_json`, and add
coverage for RSS-first delegation and the 429 backoff/retry behaviour.

fix(llm): retarget codex provider at the codex 0.136+ CLI surface

The first cut shelled out to ``codex -q -m <model> -a full-auto`` which
matched the early-2025 npm build. Codex 0.136 (the build currently
shipping under ``brew install codex`` / ``npm i -g @openai/codex``)
removed the bare-command flags entirely and replaced them with a
``codex exec`` subcommand. The old argv now exits with
``error: unexpected argument '-q' found``.

Rewrites the adapter against the new surface:

  codex exec -m <model> -s <sandbox> --skip-git-repo-check \
             --ephemeral -o <tmpfile> -

- ``codex exec`` is the non-interactive entry point; the bare command
  is interactive-only on this version.
- ``-s read-only`` sandboxes any model-generated shell commands.
  Configurable via ``sandbox_mode`` if a caller really needs writes.
- ``--skip-git-repo-check`` lets the adapter run from non-git working
  trees (TradingAgents callers may not be in a repo).
- ``--ephemeral`` skips writing a session file to ``~/.codex/sessions/``.
- ``-o <tmpfile>`` writes ONLY the final assistant reply to a file —
  much cleaner than scraping the agent loop's progress lines back out
  of stdout. The temp file is created with ``mkstemp`` and unlinked in
  a ``finally`` so a crash mid-call doesn't leak. Stdout is still
  consulted as a fallback in case a future build stops populating ``-o``.
- ``-`` as the positional prompt makes codex read instructions from
  stdin, removing the argv-length question for large
  researcher-style prompts.

Also retargets the model list at what ChatGPT-subscription auth
actually whitelists. The codex backend rejects raw API model names
(``o4-mini``, ``gpt-5``, ``gpt-5.5-mini``, ``gpt-5.5-codex``,
``gpt-5.5-pro``) with ``invalid_request_error: The '...' model is not
supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account``. Confirmed
working: ``gpt-5.4-mini`` (quick), ``gpt-5.4`` (deep balanced),
``gpt-5.5`` (deep frontier). Users running on ``OPENAI_API_KEY`` mode
can pass anything via "Custom model ID".

fundamentals: expose reporting currency and force LLM currency check

A real run on PDD (Chinese ADR) produced a confident BUY recommendation
built on a 7×-overstated margin of safety. Root cause: yfinance returned
balance-sheet and cash-flow absolute values in CNY (PDD's reporting
currency) while market cap, share price, and per-ADR EPS came back in
USD. The fundamentals analyst silently treated everything as USD,
computed "net cash per ADR = $231" (actually ¥231 ≈ $32 USD), and
concluded enterprise value was negative when in reality EV was +$92B.

Two layers of defense added so the framework can't repeat this on any
ADR of a Chinese / Japanese / European / HK / Korean company:

Data layer (dataflows/):
* y_finance.get_fundamentals: read info["financialCurrency"] and
  info["currency"], surface both at the top of the fundamentals output,
  and emit a prominent "⚠️ Currency mismatch" header when they differ
  with explicit guidance about which sections are in which currency.
* y_finance.get_balance_sheet / get_cashflow / get_income_statement:
  each statement header now includes "Reporting Currency: X" so the
  raw CSV body is unambiguously tagged.
* alpha_vantage_fundamentals: each wrapper (OVERVIEW / BALANCE_SHEET /
  CASH_FLOW / INCOME_STATEMENT) now prepends a header line extracting
  reportedCurrency from the response. String error payloads pass
  through unwrapped so vendor errors stay visible.

Prompt layer (fundamentals_styles/):
* buffett_value.py: new "LENS 0 — Currency Sanity Check" placed
  BEFORE Lens 1 with explicit required actions (state FX rate, convert
  one side, repeat converted figures in every per-share section).
  Final verdict table now includes a Currency row as a permanent
  reminder. Length cap in tests bumped 12k→14k to accommodate.
* comprehensive.py: short currency-check paragraph appended.
* growth.py: currency-check paragraph specifically calling out PEG
  (the key cross-currency ratio for growth analysis).

Tests: tests/test_currency_disclosure.py (11 new tests) covers:
* Both currencies in the yfinance header
* Mismatch warning fires on CNY/USD, absent on USD/USD
* Balance sheet / cash flow / income statement currency headers
* Alpha Vantage OVERVIEW and BALANCE_SHEET currency extraction
* Alpha Vantage string-error passthrough

fix(security): validate ticker symbols before using them as path components

Three call sites interpolate the ticker directly into a filesystem path:

- tradingagents/dataflows/stockstats_utils.py::load_ohlcv builds
  os.path.join(cache_dir, f"{symbol}-YFin-data-{start}-{end}.csv")
- tradingagents/graph/checkpointer.py::_db_path builds
  Path(data_dir) / "checkpoints" / f"{ticker.upper()}.db"
- tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py::_log_state builds
  Path(results_dir) / self.ticker / "TradingAgentsStrategy_logs"

A ticker containing path separators or "..", e.g. "../../../tmp/x",
escapes the configured cache, checkpoint, or results directory. The
ticker reaches these sites from user CLI input and from LLM tool
calls — the latter is reachable when fetched news content (yfinance,
alpha_vantage) carries prompt-injection text that steers the agent into
calling get_indicators / get_stock_data with a malicious symbol.

Add a single safe_ticker_component() helper in dataflows/utils.py that
allows only [A-Za-z0-9._^-] (covers AAPL, BRK.A, BRK-B, 0700.HK,
7203.T, ^GSPC) and rejects anything else. Apply it at each path-build
site. Existing tests use ticker="TEST" / "AAPL" / "7203.T" — all pass
the validator unchanged. Added tests/test_safe_ticker_component.py.

fix(discovery): fix infinite hang when a scanner thread blocks indefinitely

Two issues caused the agent to get stuck after the last log message
from a completed scanner (e.g. "✓ reddit_trending: 11 candidates"):

1. `as_completed()` had no global timeout. If a scanner thread blocked
   in a non-interruptible I/O call, `as_completed()` waited forever
   because it only yields a future once it has finished — the per-future
   `future.result(timeout=N)` call was never even reached.
   Fixed by passing `timeout=global_timeout` to `as_completed()` so
   the outer iterator raises TimeoutError after a capped wall-clock
   budget, then logs which scanners didn't complete and continues.

2. `SectorRotationScanner` called `get_ticker_info()` (one HTTP request
   per ticker) in a serial loop for up to 100 tickers from a 592-ticker
   file, easily exceeding the 30 s per-scanner budget.
   Fixed by batch-downloading close prices for all tickers in a single
   `download_history()` call, computing 5-day returns locally, and only
   calling `get_ticker_info()` for the small subset of laggard tickers
   (<2% 5d move) that actually need a sector label.

feat: add LangGraph checkpoint resume for crash recovery (#594)

Long analyses can take many minutes; a crash or interruption forced users
to re-run from scratch and re-pay every LLM call.  This adds an opt-in
checkpoint layer backed by per-ticker SQLite databases so the graph
resumes from the last successful node.

How to use:
- CLI:    tradingagents analyze --checkpoint
- CLI:    tradingagents analyze --clear-checkpoints
- Python: config["checkpoint_enabled"] = True

Lifecycle:
- propagate() recompiles the graph with a SqliteSaver when enabled and
  injects a deterministic thread_id derived from ticker+date so the
  same ticker+date resumes while a different date starts fresh.
- On successful completion the per-thread checkpoint rows are cleared.
- The context manager is closed in a try/finally so a crash never
  leaks the SQLite connection or leaves the graph in checkpoint mode.

Storage: ~/.tradingagents/cache/checkpoints/<TICKER>.db
(override via TRADINGAGENTS_CACHE_DIR).

The checkpointer module is new (tradingagents/graph/checkpointer.py)
and the GraphSetup now returns the uncompiled workflow so it can be
recompiled with a saver when needed.

* fix(data): normalize symbols on the identity and reflection paths

resolve_instrument_identity and the reflection return lookup queried Yahoo with
the raw ticker, so broker/forex/commodity symbols (XAUUSD, BTCUSD, EURUSD)
failed identity or could mismatch the priced instrument even though the price
path already normalized them. Route both through normalize_symbol (#983, #984).

* fix(cli): unify ticker handling with the data-path symbol normalizer

The CLI validated, normalized, and classified tickers with its own logic that
diverged from the data layer: it rejected '=' symbols like GC=F (#980),
classified BTCUSD as a stock (#981), and accepted unpriceable BTC-USDT (#982).
Route the CLI through normalize_symbol (now mapping USDT/USDC crypto quotes to
Yahoo's -USD pair), so validation, classification, and pricing agree.

* fix(data): respect the configured vendor chain and log vendor failures

The router silently extended every request to all available vendors regardless
of config, so an explicit single-vendor choice still fell back to others and
returned data from an unexpected source (#988, #289), and serious primary-vendor
errors were swallowed without a trace (#989). The configured vendor list is now
the exact chain (list several for ordered fallback; "default" uses all), unknown
vendors raise, and swallowed vendor errors are logged. Adds an autouse config
isolation fixture so vendor config can't leak between tests.

* fix(data): include the requested end date in yfinance fetches

yfinance treats end as exclusive, so get_YFin_data_online dropped the requested
end_date row and load_ohlcv dropped the current day. Request one day past the
end so the range is inclusive (look-ahead is still prevented by the curr_date
filter; the header still shows the requested range). Also correct the load_ohlcv
docstring to the 5-year window it actually downloads.

* fix(cli): correct invalid escape sequence in confirm_ollama_endpoint docstring

The docstring used \` (an invalid escape that raises SyntaxWarning and will
become a SyntaxError); use plain backticks.

* fix(data): add Alpha Vantage request timeout and stop mislabeling bad keys

Alpha Vantage requests had no timeout (a stall could hang the run) and any
notice mentioning "API key" was raised as a rate limit — so an invalid/missing
key was mislabeled and silently treated as transient. Add a 30s request timeout
and classify rate-limit phrasing before key errors (rate-limit notices also
mention "API key"), surfacing a bad key as a real configuration error.

* fix(data): keep future/undated news out of historical windows

The yfinance news date filter only ran when an article had a parsed date, so
flat-format and undated articles bypassed it and leaked future news into
historical/backtest runs. Parse the flat providerPublishTime, apply one
look-ahead-safe window rule across ticker and global news (undated kept only
when the window reaches the present), and return an informative message when
everything is filtered out.

* fix(graph): register get_verified_market_snapshot in the market ToolNode

The market analyst is bound to call get_verified_market_snapshot and its prompt
requires it as the source of truth, but the tool was missing from the market
ToolNode executor — so the call failed and the model reported it "unavailable"
and skipped verification. Register it (with a regression guard) so the snapshot
actually runs and grounds the report.

* feat(llm): unify OpenAI-compatible providers behind a registry + generic endpoint

The OpenAI-compatible family (openai, xAI, DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM, MiniMax,
OpenRouter, Ollama) all speak the same Chat Completions API and differ only by
base_url, key, and two narrow wire-format quirks already isolated in subclasses.
Replace the scattered base-URL dict, key handling, and client-class branches with
one ProviderSpec registry that get_llm and the factory drive off; provider quirks
stay in their subclasses. Add a generic "openai_compatible" provider for any
OpenAI-compatible server (vLLM, LM Studio, llama.cpp, relays) via backend_url +
optional key — adding a provider is now one registry row. Native Anthropic/Google
keep their own clients (genuinely different APIs). Also fixes the env backend URL
being ignored when the provider was chosen interactively (#978).

Surface Federal Reserve Economic Data (rates, inflation, labor, growth) to the
news analyst via a new get_macro_indicators tool and a macro_data vendor
category. Friendly aliases (cpi, unemployment, fed_funds_rate, 10y_treasury,
yield_curve, ...) map to FRED series IDs; raw series IDs are accepted too. The
report gives the latest value, change over the window, and a recent observation
table. Windowing is lookahead-safe (observation_end = curr_date), missing values
are skipped, and a missing FRED_API_KEY surfaces as a clear not-configured
condition through the vendor router rather than a crash.

* feat(data): add Polymarket prediction markets as a keyless vendor

Surface live, market-implied probabilities for forward-looking events (Fed
decisions, recession, elections, geopolitics, crypto) to the news analyst via a
new get_prediction_markets tool and a prediction_markets vendor category. Backed
by Polymarket's public Gamma API (no key). Results are filtered to open,
forward-looking markets (closed and past-dated events excluded), ranked by
traded volume, and rendered with implied probability, volume, resolution date,
and the recent move. External errors degrade to a clear unavailable message
rather than interrupting the analyst.

* refactor(data): unify vendor errors under a VendorError hierarchy

Every condition where a vendor cannot return usable data now derives from a
single VendorError base (errors.py): NoMarketDataError, VendorRateLimitError,
and VendorNotConfiguredError (still a ValueError for back-compat). Vendor-named
errors subclass the generic bases, and the router catches the base types, so a
new vendor needs no new except clause. Not-configured now has explicit
try-next-vendor handling instead of falling through the generic catch-all. The
number of error types tracks the number of distinct router reactions, not the
number of causes.

* fix(data): reject stale yfinance OHLCV instead of reporting wrong prices

yfinance intermittently returns a year-old partial frame (e.g. June 2025 rows
for a June 2026 request) that still has rows and a Close, so it passed the
empty-check and silently fed a wrong close price and indicators into the report
(#1021). Add a freshness guard that rejects a frame whose latest row is far
older than the requested date, on both the raw OHLCV path and the indicator
path. It raises the existing NoMarketDataError with a stale-specific detail, so
the vendor router's try-next-vendor and single unavailable-signal handling apply
unchanged; the sentinel now surfaces that detail so the agent reports the
specific reason rather than fabricating a value.

* fix(reddit): go RSS-first with 429 backoff and robust transport errors

The JSON search endpoint is reliably WAF-blocked (403) for public clients, so
probing it on every call doubled request volume against Reddit's per-IP rate
limit and tripped 429 on the RSS fallback, blanking the sentiment feed. Fetch
the Atom/RSS feed directly (JSON kept as an opt-in path that still degrades to
RSS on 403), back off once on a 429 honouring Retry-After, and pace requests a
little wider. Also broaden the error handling to catch http.client chunked
transfer errors (IncompleteRead/BadStatusLine) alongside OSError, which on their
own slipped through and crashed the pipeline.

* fix(data): catch http.client transport errors in StockTwits

A truncated/incomplete chunked response raises http.client exceptions
(IncompleteRead/BadStatusLine) that are not OSErrors, so they bypassed the
existing handler and crashed the analysis. Broaden the catch so the fetch
degrades to its placeholder string like every other transport failure.

feat(llm): add codex provider via the local Codex CLI subprocess

Mirrors the claude-code provider's shape for users who want to drive
TradingAgents off whatever auth the local `codex` CLI is already
configured with (ChatGPT subscription via `codex --login` on recent
builds, or `OPENAI_API_KEY` on older ones). Unlike claude-code which
ships a Python SDK with structured message types, codex is only
distributed as a Node CLI, so this adapter is a thin subprocess
wrapper around `codex -q -m <model> -a full-auto`. The `-q` flag
suppresses intermediate reasoning / tool-call narration; `-a full-auto`
keeps the agent loop from blocking on permission prompts in
non-interactive use; `--no-project-doc` keeps a stray `codex.md` in
cwd from silently changing model behaviour.

Scope is pure chat. `bind_tools` raises `NotImplementedError` —
codex runs its own internal tool-use loop with built-in Bash / file
operations and has no documented hook for LangChain tool descriptors
the way `claude_agent_sdk.create_sdk_mcp_server` does for claude-code.
`with_structured_output` likewise raises so the project's existing
`bind_structured` helper transparently degrades manager / trader /
portfolio-manager to free-text generation. Analyst nodes that use
`bind_tools` must stay on a key-based provider (or claude-code).

Failure modes are surfaced as `RuntimeError` with actionable context:
codex binary missing on PATH, codex nonzero exit (CLI's stderr is
included verbatim, capped at 500 chars), empty stdout, or
`TimeoutExpired` past the configurable `timeout_s` (default 600s).
`shutil.which("codex")` is checked at `get_llm()` so a misconfigured
environment fails before the graph starts spending tokens elsewhere.

Wires through `factory.py` (`provider == "codex"`), `api_key_env.py`
(no env-var check — auth owned by the CLI), and `model_catalog.py`
(a representative `quick` / `deep` split using o4-mini / o4 / o3 /
gpt-5; "Custom model ID" surfaces anything else the user's account
is entitled to).

21 new unit tests cover message flattening, factory wiring (including
the up-front `shutil.which` check), phase-1 contracts
(bind_tools / with_structured_output must raise so the structured
fallback fires), argv construction, and every `_generate` error path
(nonzero exit, empty stdout, FileNotFoundError -> RuntimeError,
TimeoutExpired -> RuntimeError, empty prompt short-circuit). All paths
mock `subprocess.run` so CI does not need codex installed.

fix(scanner): resolve scan_date fan-in drop, run_id propagation, and NO_EVIDENCE summarizers

## Summary
Three compounding bugs caused scanner runs to crash with `KeyError: 'scan_date'` and
all summarizer nodes to produce `[NO_EVIDENCE]` despite upstream scanners returning data.
Root cause: `scan_date` had no LangGraph reducer so it was dropped at fan-in merge boundaries;
`run_id` was absent from ScannerState entirely so disk-based idempotency couldn't resolve
artifact paths; and scanner_summarizer didn't fall back to disk when state fields were empty
after a BFS super-step merge.

## Changes
- `scanner_states.py`: added `_last_value` reducer to `scan_date`; added `run_id: Annotated[str, _last_value]` as a proper state field — previously it was invisible to LangGraph fan-in merges
- `scanner_idempotency.py`: introduced `_state_run_id()` which falls back to the active `RunLogger` ContextVar when `state.get("run_id")` is None; `check_and_load_report` and `save_node_report` now use it
- `scanner_summarizer.py`: disk fallback in raw report fetch — `state.get(report_key, "") or check_and_load_report(state, report_key) or ""` so BFS super-step state gaps don't produce false NO_EVIDENCE
- `industry_deep_dive.py` / `macro_synthesis.py`: defensive `state.get("scan_date") or time.strftime(...)` instead of hard `state["scan_date"]` key access
- `langgraph_engine.py`: `_load_scan_state` now includes `run_id`; `run_scan_from_node` force-sets `scan_date` and `run_id` after `**initial_state` unpack to prevent stale rerun state overriding them
- `trading_graph.py`: added `Dict, List, Optional, Set` to typing import — fixed `NameError` on startup
- Tests: 5 new test files / extensions covering all of the above

## Decision Context
- LangGraph fan-in (multiple predecessors → single node): plain TypedDict fields not annotated with a reducer get silently dropped in the merged state snapshot; `Annotated[str, _last_value]` prevents this
- LangGraph BFS super-step: all Phase 1a scanners (gatekeeper, geopolitical, market_movers, sector) form one super-step; their summarizers form the next; during the gap, each summarizer sees an empty string for other scanners' reports because LangGraph accumulates state via reducer, not broadcast — this is why the disk fallback is needed
- `asyncio.to_thread` copies ContextVar; LangGraph uses `copy_context().run()` so `RunLogger` ContextVar IS accessible inside node threads — the `_state_run_id()` RunLogger fallback is safe to use
- Force-override of `scan_date` / `run_id` after `**initial_state` unpack in `run_scan_from_node`: reconstructed partial-rerun state loaded from disk may have a blank `scan_date` from an older format; explicit assignment wins over dict merge order

## Considerations for Future Agents
- Any new ScannerState field that must survive fan-in merges MUST use `Annotated[str, _last_value]` — plain `str` fields will be dropped silently; this is the #1 footgun in this codebase
- The disk fallback in `scanner_summarizer.py` only works if `save_node_report` is called inside each scanner node after it produces its report AND before the super-step ends — verify scanners call `save_node_report` in their own node functions
- Fresh scan run needed to confirm NO_EVIDENCE is fully resolved end-to-end; the fix chain is: scanner saves file → summarizer loads from disk → summarizer invokes LLM → summary propagates to Phase 2
- `run_id` field added to ScannerState may need to be seeded in any test fixtures that create ScannerState snapshots for partial-rerun testing

feat: add MiniMax (Global + China) as built-in LLM providers

Wire MiniMax into the existing OpenAI-compatible provider path. Two
separate provider keys instead of one, because MiniMax operates two
independent regional services with different account systems:

  - minimax     -> https://api.minimax.io/v1   (Global, MINIMAX_API_KEY)
  - minimax-cn  -> https://api.minimaxi.com/v1 (China,  MINIMAX_CN_API_KEY)

Keys issued on one region don't authenticate against the other, so
hiding the regional split behind a single 'minimax' key would silently
fail with a 401 the moment a CN user picked it from the picker. Two
explicit entries make the choice discoverable in the CLI and self-
documenting in README.

Featured models (identical catalog on both regions):
  - MiniMax-M2.7              flagship, SOTA on coding + agent
                              benchmarks, 204K context, ~60 TPS
  - MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed    same quality, ~100 TPS
                              (good fit for the quick-think slot)
  - MiniMax-M2.5              previous-gen flagship, kept as fallback

Why this fits TradingAgents:
  - 204K context handles a full earnings call + 10-K excerpts in one
    pass, no chunking needed
  - Strong tool-use keeps the multi-agent debate stable across rounds
  - Highspeed variant pairs the quick-think slot without sacrificing
    the deep-think reasoning quality

Changes:

                      base URL + API-key env var
  - model_catalog.py  add identical model lists for both providers
  - cli/utils.py      add 'MiniMax' and 'MiniMax CN' to the picker
  - .env.example      add MINIMAX_API_KEY and MINIMAX_CN_API_KEY
  - README.md         add both env vars, list both in the provider

                      comment

fix(options_flow): scan full universe before applying limit, rank by signal strength

Previously the scanner stopped as soon as self.limit candidates were found
from as_completed() futures. Since futures complete in non-deterministic
network-latency order, this was equivalent to random sampling — fast-to-
respond tickers won regardless of how strong their options signal was.

Fix: collect all candidates from the full universe, then sort by options_score
(unusual strike count weighted 1.5x for calls to favor bullish flow) before
applying the limit. The top-N strongest signals are now always returned.

fix(filter): only filter upside intraday movers, not downside

The same-day mover filter used abs() to check intraday movement, which
filtered both gap-ups AND gap-downs. On volatile/crash days (e.g. 2026-04-07)
all stocks dropped >10% from open, causing every candidate to be filtered and
leaving zero recommendations.

The filter's purpose is to avoid chasing stocks that already ran up. A stock
down 20% intraday is not "stale" — it should be evaluated on its merits.
Changed threshold check from abs(pct) >= threshold to pct >= threshold so only
upside movers are filtered.

fix(graph): don't reprint unchanged trailing message in debug stream

In debug mode `_run_graph` calls `chunk["messages"][-1].pretty_print()` for
every streamed chunk. LangGraph emits a chunk per node, but `messages` only
grows when a node appends one — so the same trailing message (e.g. the
trader's final proposal) is reprinted across every subsequent node, producing
~5×-duplicated blocks in the debug log.

Track the last-printed message signature and only pretty_print when it
changes. The returned state is unaffected: every chunk is still appended to
`trace` and merged into `final_state`; only the console output is de-duped.

feat(app): /analyze + /stream — wrap TradingAgents with HTTP + SSE

Implements the user-facing endpoints for the Lyceum Fund Python service.
After this lands, the Node-side worker can POST /analyze to kick off a
TradingAgents run, and the dashboard can subscribe to /stream/{runId}
for live per-agent progress.

Architecture:
- app/services/trading_agents_runner.py orchestrates a run end-to-end —
  constructs TradingAgentsGraph (with memory_log_path=None to disable
  upstream file persistence), bypasses propagate() to control the
  astream() loop, injects a LangChain callback that writes agent_reports
  rows + publishes events to Redis pub-sub.
- app/services/callbacks.py — AsyncCallbackHandler. on_chain_start fires
  agent_started event, on_chain_end persists the chains output to
  agent_reports + fires agent_finished. Heuristic name normalizer drops
  Chain/Agent suffixes from serialized chain names.
- app/services/pubsub.py — generic Redis pub-sub helpers. Channel
  convention run:<runId>. DONE_SENTINEL marks stream end.
- app/services/stream_token.py — HMAC-signed compact tokens for SSE auth.
  Format: base64url(payload).hex(hmac_sha256(payload, HMAC_SHARED_SECRET))
  with payload {runId, exp}. Browser EventSource cant send headers so
  the query-param token replaces HMAC headers for browser streams.
- app/routes/analyze.py — POST /analyze. HMAC-auth via existing
  middleware. Idempotent on runId so Node-side retries dont duplicate.
  Schedules a FastAPI BackgroundTask; returns 202 immediately.
- app/routes/stream.py — GET /stream/{run_id}?token=... SSE feed. Token
  verified server-side. Subscribes to Redis pub-sub, forwards each
  event as data: <json> records. Closes on DONE_SENTINEL with an
  event: close record.

v1 uses FastAPI BackgroundTasks for the analyze pipeline — see TT-286
for the planned migration to a dedicated Arq worker service when
restart-safety + concurrency limits matter.

fix: cash_sweep target_cash_pct from config, defaults to min_cash_pct

Audit finding (Important): cash_sweep hardcoded target_cash_pct=0.05 while
min_cash_pct is config-driven. A deployment that raised min_cash_pct (e.g.
to 0.10) would have its operator-intent silently violated — sweep would
keep pushing cash toward the 5% target, leaving the reserve below intent.
The hard floor was never breached, but the soft target no longer matched
the deployed policy.

Fix: target_cash_pct = float(config.get("target_cash_pct", min_cash_pct)).
Defaulting to min_cash_pct keeps the soft target tied to the hard floor;
operators may still set target_cash_pct > min_cash_pct for a buffer.

fix(y_finance): make suppress_yfinance_warnings thread-safe

The previous implementation redirected sys.stderr to /dev/null using a
context manager. This is not thread-safe: 8 concurrent scanner threads each
mutate sys.stderr, and when one thread's context manager closes the devnull
file, another thread that captured devnull as its saved stderr attempts to
write to the closed fd and raises "I/O operation on closed file".

This corrupted sys.stderr state caused _fetch_batch_prices to fail and
all per-ticker get_stock_price fallback calls to return None, resulting in
every candidate being dropped with "no data available".

Fix by suppressing at the Python logging level instead of redirecting
sys.stderr. Logger.setLevel() is protected by internal locks and is safe
to call from concurrent threads.

fix(ui): fix signal cards rendering as raw HTML in Streamlit

Two bugs were causing the signal card HTML to display as literal text:

1. CommonMark HTML block termination: Streamlit's markdown parser
   (CommonMark-compliant) terminates a <div> block at the first blank
   line. Empty optional fields (name_html, desc_html, risk_badge_html)
   left whitespace-only lines in the f-string template, ending the HTML
   block and causing the parser to render subsequent tags as text.
   Fixed by building HTML from a parts list and only appending optional
   elements when non-empty — no blank lines can appear in output.

2. Unescaped HTML chars in LLM-generated text: reason fields from the
   ranker contained raw > and & characters (e.g. '>5% move',
   '50 & 200 SMA') that corrupted the HTML structure. Fixed by running
   all LLM-generated fields through html.escape() before interpolation.

Fix Pregel.stream() 'multiple values for config' error

_patched_invoke was calling graph.stream(state, config_arg or {}, **kwargs).
When async_propagate passes config as a keyword argument in **args,
kwargs already contains 'config', so passing config_arg positionally
(which maps to stream's 'config' parameter) caused:
  TypeError: Pregel.stream() got multiple values for argument 'config'

Fix: merge config_arg into kwargs['config'] when needed, then call
graph.stream(state, **kwargs) — config is always passed once as keyword.

fix(dataflows): handle yfinance >=1.4 unnamed-index column

`yf.download(..., multi_level_index=False)` in yfinance 1.4+ returns
a DataFrame whose index is unnamed, so `data.reset_index()` produces
a column called `index` rather than `Date`. _clean_dataframe and the
downstream stockstats wrap then fail with KeyError('Date'), and every
technical indicator call falls back to N/A — the Market Analyst's
report is left without any 50/200 SMA, MACD, RSI, Bollinger Bands or
ATR data, silently degrading agent decision quality.

This patch renames the unnamed index column to `Date` in both the
download path (load_ohlcv) and the read-from-cache path
(_clean_dataframe), covering pre-existing cache files written by
older yfinance versions. The candidate-name loop also handles
`Datetime` (older yfinance behavior) and lowercase `date`.

Fix WS race condition: buffer events for late-connecting clients

Race condition: background analysis fails fast (e.g. 'NVIDIA_API_KEY
not set' raises in ~1s) and sends WS error event before the frontend
has had time to open the WebSocket connection. The error event was
dropped on the floor; the client connected to a silent, already-closed
channel and stayed stuck on 'Analiz Ediliyor...' forever.

Fix: WebSocketManager now maintains a per-task event buffer (deque,
max 64 events). Every send() appends to the buffer AND broadcasts to
active connections. When a client connects(), buffered events are
replayed immediately. After close_task(), the buffer is kept for 30s
(configurable via _BUFFER_TTL) so a client that connects after the
task is already finished still receives the complete event history
including the error/complete terminal event.

The buffer is cleaned up automatically via asyncio.call_later so there
is no memory leak for abandoned tasks.

Also included: global toast notification system (notify helper +
Layout toast stack + Analysis WS error → notify + axios 5xx → notify)

fix(discovery): fix infinite hang when a scanner thread blocks indefinitely

Two issues caused the agent to get stuck after the last log message
from a completed scanner (e.g. "✓ reddit_trending: 11 candidates"):

1. `as_completed()` had no global timeout. If a scanner thread blocked
   in a non-interruptible I/O call, `as_completed()` waited forever
   because it only yields a future once it has finished — the per-future
   `future.result(timeout=N)` call was never even reached.
   Fixed by passing `timeout=global_timeout` to `as_completed()` so
   the outer iterator raises TimeoutError after a capped wall-clock
   budget, then logs which scanners didn't complete and continues.

2. `SectorRotationScanner` called `get_ticker_info()` (one HTTP request
   per ticker) in a serial loop for up to 100 tickers from a 592-ticker
   file, easily exceeding the 30 s per-scanner budget.
   Fixed by batch-downloading close prices for all tickers in a single
   `download_history()` call, computing 5-day returns locally, and only
   calling `get_ticker_info()` for the small subset of laggard tickers
   (<2% 5d move) that actually need a sector label.

feat: Separate embedding configuration from chat model configuration

This commit implements a comprehensive solution for separating embedding
and chat model configurations, enabling flexible provider combinations
and graceful handling of embedding failures.

## Problem Statement

Previously, the TradingAgents memory system used the same backend_url for
both chat models and embeddings. This caused critical failures when:

- Using OpenRouter for chat (doesn't support OpenAI embedding endpoints)
- Using Anthropic/Google for chat (don't provide embeddings)
- The embedding endpoint returned HTML error pages instead of JSON
- Users wanted to mix providers (e.g., OpenRouter chat + OpenAI embeddings)

Error example:
  AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'data'
  # Caused by: OpenRouter returned HTML page instead of embedding JSON

## Solution

Implemented three key features:

1. **Separate Embedding Client Configuration**
   - New config parameters independent of chat LLM settings
   - embedding_provider: "openai", "ollama", or "none"
   - embedding_backend_url: Separate API endpoint
   - embedding_model: Specific model to use
   - enable_memory: Boolean flag to enable/disable memory

2. **Multiple Provider Support**
   - OpenAI: Production-grade embeddings (recommended)
   - Ollama: Local embeddings for offline/development
   - None: Disable memory system entirely

3. **Graceful Fallback**
   - System continues when embeddings fail
   - Comprehensive error logging
   - Memory operations return empty results instead of crashing
   - Agents function without historical context when memory disabled

## Changes

### Core Framework
- tradingagents/default_config.py: Added 4 new embedding config params
- tradingagents/agents/utils/memory.py: Complete refactor with error handling
- tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py: Separated embedding initialization

### CLI/User Interface
- cli/utils.py: Added select_embedding_provider() function
- cli/main.py: Added Step 7 for embedding provider selection

### Documentation (New Files)
- docs/EMBEDDING_CONFIGURATION.md: Complete usage guide (381 lines)
- docs/EMBEDDING_MIGRATION.md: Implementation details (374 lines)
- CHANGELOG_EMBEDDING.md: Release notes (225 lines)
- FEATURE_EMBEDDING_README.md: Branch overview (418 lines)

### Testing & Verification
- tests/test_embedding_config.py: Comprehensive test suite
- verify_config.py: Simple config verification script

## Example Usage

```python
# OpenRouter for chat, OpenAI for embeddings
config = {
    "llm_provider": "openrouter",
    "backend_url": "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1",
    "deep_think_llm": "deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3-0324:free",

    "embedding_provider": "openai",
    "embedding_backend_url": "https://api.openai.com/v1",
    "embedding_model": "text-embedding-3-small",
    "enable_memory": True,
}
```

## Backward Compatibility

✅ 100% Backward Compatible - No breaking changes!

Existing configurations work without modification. Smart defaults
applied when embedding settings are omitted.

## Testing

- All core files pass diagnostics with no errors
- Configuration verification script passes all checks
- Supports scenarios: OpenRouter+OpenAI, All Ollama, Disabled Memory
- Graceful fallback tested for invalid URLs and missing API keys

## Benefits

- Enables using OpenRouter/other providers for chat
- Reduces costs (can use local embeddings or disable memory)
- Improves reliability (graceful degradation on failures)
- Maintains full backward compatibility
- Comprehensive documentation and examples

fix(discovery): fix three scanner hang/validation bugs found in ranker_debug.log

1. executor.shutdown(wait=True) still blocked after global timeout (critical)
   The previous fix added timeout= to as_completed() but used `with
   ThreadPoolExecutor() as executor`, whose __exit__ calls shutdown(wait=True).
   This meant the process still hung waiting for stuck threads (ml_signal) even
   after the TimeoutError was caught.  Fixed by creating the executor explicitly
   and calling shutdown(wait=False) in a finally block.

2. ml_signal hangs on every run — "Batch-downloading 592 tickers (1y)..." never
   completes. Root cause: a single yfinance request for 592 tickers × 1 year of
   daily OHLCV is a very large payload that regularly times out at the network
   layer. Fixed by:
   - Reducing default lookback from "1y" to "6mo" (halves download size)
   - Splitting downloads into 150-ticker chunks so a slow chunk doesn't kill
     the whole scan (partial results are still returned)

3. C (Citigroup) and other single-letter NYSE tickers rejected as invalid.
   validate_ticker_format used ^[A-Z]{2,5}$ requiring at least 2 letters.
   Real tickers like C, A, F, T, X, M are 1 letter. Fixed to ^[A-Z]{1,5}$.

feat(ui): scoped graph nodes per ticker + MockEngine for LLM-free UI testing (#100)

* feat(ui): scoped graph nodes per ticker + MockEngine for LLM-free UI testing

## Summary
Adds a MockEngine that streams scripted agent events with zero real LLM calls,
enabling full UI testing (graph, terminal, drawer, metrics) without API keys or
network. Also fixes the ReactFlow graph so that each ticker/identifier gets its
own visual node — previously an auto run with 5 tickers collapsed all pipelines
into the same node IDs, overwriting each other.

## Changes
- **MockEngine** (`agent_os/backend/services/mock_engine.py`): new class that
  generates realistic scripted events for pipeline, scan, and auto run types.
  Supports configurable speed divisor (1× realistic → 10× instant). Auto mock
  accepts a `tickers` list for multi-ticker runs.
- **POST /api/run/mock** (`runs.py`): new endpoint wiring MockEngine into the
  BackgroundTasks + store pattern identical to real run endpoints.
- **WebSocket routing** (`websocket.py`): added `mock` run-type branch so the
  WS executor path also dispatches to MockEngine when the background task hasn't
  started yet.
- **LangGraphEngine** (`langgraph_engine.py`): added `_run_identifiers` dict to
  track ticker/MARKET/portfolio_id per run; all emitted events now carry an
  `identifier` field so the frontend can scope them.
- **AgentGraph.tsx**: ReactFlow nodes now keyed by `node_id:identifier` (e.g.
  `news_analyst:AAPL`, `news_analyst:NVDA`). Edges scoped to same identifier.
  `onNodeClick` passes raw `node_id` + `identifier` separately so the event
  drawer can filter without parsing the scoped key.
- **Dashboard.tsx**: Mock button + type/speed controls added. `openNodeDetail`
  accepts identifier; `NodeEventsDetail` filters by both `node_id` and
  `identifier`. Comma-separated ticker input for mock auto runs (e.g.
  `AAPL,NVDA,TSLA`).
- **useAgentStream.ts**: `AgentEvent` interface extended with `identifier?`
  field.

## Decision Context
- Scoped node ID format chosen as `node_id:identifier` (colon separator) rather
  than embedding identifier in the agent display name — keeps node labels clean
  and identifier visible as a coloured badge, not label text.
- Raw `node_id` and `identifier` stored separately in `node.data` so the drawer
  filtering (`events.filter(e => e.node_id === nodeId && e.identifier === id)`)
  does not need to parse/split the scoped key.
- Parent edges are scoped to the same identifier as the child, assuming intra-
  ticker chains. Cross-run topology edges (e.g. scan → pipeline) are implicit
  via log events, not ReactFlow edges.
- MockEngine uses `asyncio.sleep` with a speed divisor — higher speed values
  give faster replays for rapid iteration during UI development.

## Considerations for Future Agents
- Re-run button on graph nodes already uses `identifier` to dispatch
  `startRun('pipeline', { ticker: identifier })` or `startRun('scan')` — no
  further changes needed for per-node re-runs to be correctly scoped.
- The `_run_identifiers` dict in LangGraphEngine is keyed by `run_id`; it is
  cleaned up after each run. If parallel runs are ever supported per engine
  instance, this dict handles them correctly already.
- For run_auto, each sub-run (scan, per-ticker pipeline) calls its own
  `run_scan`/`run_pipeline` which sets `_run_identifiers[run_id]`. The outer
  `run_auto` does not set it — this is intentional.
- `uv.lock` changes reflect dependency tree after Chainlit removal in the
  previous commit; no new runtime dependencies were added by this PR.

fix: harden dataflows layer against silent failures and data corruption

## Problem (Incident Post-mortem)

The pipeline was emitting hundreds of errors:
  'Invalid number of return arguments after parsing column name: Date'

Root cause: after _clean_dataframe() lowercases all columns, stockstats.wrap()
promotes 'date' to the DataFrame index. Subsequent df['Date'] access caused
stockstats to try parsing 'Date' as a technical indicator name.

## Fixes

### 1. Fix df['Date'] stockstats bug (already shipped in prior commit)
- stockstats_utils.py + y_finance.py: use df.index.strftime() instead of
  df['Date'] after wrap()

### 2. Extract _load_or_fetch_ohlcv() — single OHLCV authority
- Eliminates duplicated 30-line download+cache boilerplate in two places
- Cache filename is always derived from today's date — hardcoded stale date
  '2015-01-01-2025-03-25' in local mode is gone
- Corruption/truncation detection: files <50 rows or unparseable are deleted
  and re-fetched rather than silently returning bad data
- Drops on_bad_lines='skip' — malformed CSVs now raise instead of silently
  dropping rows that would distort indicator calculations

### 3. YFinanceError typed exception
- Defined in stockstats_utils.py; raised instead of print()+return ''
- get_stockstats_indicator now raises YFinanceError on failure so errors
  surface to callers rather than delivering empty strings to LLM agents
- interface.py route_to_vendor now catches YFinanceError alongside
  AlphaVantageError and FinnhubError — failures appear in observability
  telemetry and can trigger vendor fallback

### 4. Explicit date column discovery in alpha_vantage_common
- _filter_csv_by_date_range: replaced df.columns[0] positional assumption
  with explicit search for 'time'/'timestamp'/'date' column
- ValueError re-raised (not swallowed) so bad API response shape is visible

### 5. Structured logging
- Replaced all print() calls in changed files with logging.getLogger()
- Added logging import + logger to alpha_vantage_common

## Tests
- tests/unit/test_incident_fixes.py: 12 new unit tests covering all fixes
  (dynamic cache filename, corruption re-fetch, YFinanceError propagation,
  explicit column lookup, empty download raises)
- tests/integration/test_stockstats_live.py: 11 live tests against real
  yfinance API (all major indicators, weekend N/A, regression guard)
- All 70 tests pass (59 unit + 11 live integration)
